en: The four questions count together
Answer the four questions in order. If every answer is yes, your case falls within the category. If any answer is no, the law still protects you.
<1><2>1.</2> Can what was promised be identified?</1><3>The utility that was sold, not slogans or lists of decorations</3><4><5>p. 428</5></4>
<1>no<2>, go to the last box</2></1>
<1><2>2.</2> Did the purchase open a place that lasts?</1><3>A position that has to keep existing for the thing to be of use</3><4><5>p. 428</5></4>
<1><2>3.</2> Does the platform govern that place?</1><3>Internal rules, choices about what is shown, and penalties</3><4><5>p. 428</5></4>
<1><2>4.</2> Can it get worse without disappearing?</1><3>Access continues, but what you had is downgraded or emptied</3><4><5>p. 429</5></4>
<1>Your case falls within the category</1><2>The rights the Path explains from here on apply</2><3><4>p. 429</4></3>

<1>The law still protects you</1><2>The case falls outside the category and follows the general rules, as with an undue charge, an isolated defect or a one-off misleading ad</2><3><4>p. 433-435</4></3>
This is a screening, not a ruling. What decides is finding all four at the same time, not the impression that technology is somewhere in between. <1><2>p. 429</2></1>

The four fields are the gateway to the eleven situations
The four fields must be present at the same time. If they are, the regime applies. If one is missing, the case is outside the IOC and ordinary protection continues.
<1>Object promised as an enjoyment bundle</1><2>The utility offered in functions and meanings, identifiable</2><3><4>p. 428</4></3>
<1>Sustained position of enjoyment</1><2>The acquisition opens a position that has to remain</2><3><4>p. 428</4></3>
<1>Infrastructural governance</1><2>Internal criteria and enforcement mechanisms as the way supply is performed</2><3><4>p. 428</4></3>
<1>Relevant degradation without total rupture</1><2>Enjoyment formally continues, but is downgraded, emptied or reconfigured</2><3><4>p. 429</4></3>
<1>all present</1><2>one missing</2>
all present
<1>The regime applies</1><2>The eleven situations, a to k, apply the CDC from the qualification of the object</2><3><4>p. 429</4></3>
one missing
<1>Outside the IOC, ordinary protection continues</1><2>The five exclusion limits</2><3><4>p. 433-435</4></3>
One-off access without a sustained position<1><2>p. 433</2></1>
Channel or storefront that does not govern the utility<1><2>p. 434</2></1>
Symbolic value ancillary to the core of the bundle<1><2>p. 434</2></1>
Ordinary variations of the ecosystem<1><2>p. 434</2></1>
A conflict whose core is something else<1><2>p. 435</2></1>
Application is decided by the cumulative presence of verifiable elements, not by technological intuition or deference to the contract. <1><2>p. 429</2></1>

As a filter, it defines what comes in and what stays outside the field of application, preventing any digital relationship with an appearance of continuity from being absorbed by the category and also preventing the supplier from expelling the conflict from the CDC through strategic labelling<1>p. 428</1>
The point is to delimit the zone in which enjoyment formally continues to exist but is downgraded, emptied or reconfigured<1>p. 429</1>
The third limit concerns situations in which the symbolic or semiotic value is functionally ancillary and is not part of the core of the promised enjoyment bundle.<1>p. 434</1>

The fourth limit covers ordinary variations of the ecosystem that do not amount to relevant and persistent degradation of the bundle, such as updates, interface adjustments, anti-abuse measures, regular moderation and occasional instability.<1>p. 434</1>
